clue.text: In dialect, spoken literature doesn't follow

indicators.note: in some regional accents the vowel of one word is said like another, so the clue word is heard rather than written

parts.note: books are literature

explanation.surface: A remark on regional speech where literary works trail behind the talk.
explanation.walkthrough: In some northern English accents BOOKS rhymes with BUCKS, which 'In dialect, spoken' asks you to hear.
explanation.definitionFit: To buck a trend is to refuse to go along with it, so it means declining to follow.

clue.text: No leads chewed, tie up

parts.note: bit is the past tense of bite, so chewed

indicators.note: in a down entry, up means the word for tie is read backwards

parts.note: to strap is to tie

explanation.surface: Someone without dog leads chews through ties instead.
explanation.walkthrough: 'No leads' looks like dog leashes but means acting roles that are not the lead.
explanation.definitionFit: Minor roles in a play or film are those that are not leading roles.

clue.text: Escape cold and warm up

parts.note: C is the abbreviation for cold, as on a tap
to heat something is to warm it up

explanation.surface: Instructions to get out of the cold and thaw.
explanation.definitionFit: To cheat death or fate is to escape it narrowly.

clue.text: Highly personal reality TV script re-written

indicators.note: a script that is rewritten has its letters reworked into a new order

explanation.surface: A reality show's script gets rewritten to be very intimate.
explanation.definitionFit: Something wholly confidential and intimate is very personal indeed.

clue.text: Modest about power and Tory protection

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the word for modest goes around the letter for power

parts.note: coy means shy or modest
P is the physics symbol for power
Tories are on the political right

explanation.surface: A shy politician seeks power and Conservative cover.
explanation.definitionFit: Legal ownership of creative work shields it from copying, a form of legal protection.

clue.text: Motorcade struggles to keep parking alongside

indicators.note: to keep is to hold within, so the jumbled letters enclose the parking sign
a motorcade that struggles is thrown into disorder, so its letters are rearranged

parts.note: P is the road sign abbreviation for parking

explanation.surface: A procession of cars has trouble finding parking spaces side by side.
explanation.definitionFit: Set beside something for comparison, as in 'small set against the other'.

clue.text: When a duke's packing, I should add notebooks

indicators.note: packing means holding inside, so the postscript surrounds the other letters

parts.note: a PS or postscript is what a letter writer adds as an afterthought

explanation.surface: A traveller notes that when the duke packs, extra notebooks should go in.
explanation.walkthrough: 'I should add' is the sense of a postscript, PS.
explanation.definitionFit: Writing pads are bound sheets of paper for jotting, much like notebooks.

clue.text: After he's upset?

parts.note: the letters of the eight-letter plumage word, jumbled up (ruffled), spell out these two clue words

explanation.surface: A question about what happens once a man gets annoyed.
explanation.walkthrough: Read the answer as an instruction: ruffle the letters of FEATHERS and you get AFTER HE'S, the clue's own words.
explanation.definitionFit: Ruffled plumage is an idiom for irritation or annoyance caused to someone.

clue.text: Travel across lake and promise to shorten travel

indicators.note: across means stretched over, so the verb for travel spans the letter for lake

parts.note: to go is to travel
L is the map abbreviation for lake

indicators.note: the word for promise is cut short, losing its last letter

parts.note: to betroth is to promise in marriage

explanation.surface: Advice on crossing a lake and cutting a journey short.
explanation.definitionFit: To roam widely around the world is to travel extensively.

clue.text: Able to stand, cheers the greatest

parts.note: ta is British slang for thanks, like cheers
a king is the greatest, as in the king of the castle

explanation.surface: A toast to a champion who can still stand up.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who can take it is able to endure; the verb take means bear or withstand.

clue.text: Sleep on Kojak's idea

parts.note: Theo Kojak is the bald detective of the 1970s TV series Kojak
REM is rapid eye movement sleep

explanation.surface: The TV detective's notion came to him in his sleep.
explanation.definitionFit: A proposition in mathematics is a formal idea that can be proved.

clue.text: Ornament from slices cut from cloth

indicators.note: slices means cuts into, so the short word for from goes inside the word for ornament

parts.note: to deck is to adorn or ornament
fro is an old word meaning from, as in to and fro

explanation.surface: A decoration made from strips of fabric.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cloth' is the clergy: to be cut from the cloth is to be thrown out of the priesthood.
explanation.definitionFit: Stripping a priest of office removes them from the clergy, known as the cloth.

clue.text: Not For Tea — unknown Huxley novel

parts.note: anti means against, not for
cha or char is slang for tea
Y is an algebra unknown

explanation.surface: A book title that sounds like a refusal of afternoon tea.
explanation.definitionFit: Aldous Huxley's 1923 satirical book is called Antic Hay.

clue.text: Tell wicked uncle about one

indicators.note: about means around, so the jumbled letters surround the numeral
a wicked uncle is a twisted one, so its letters are rearranged

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: A child is urged to reveal a nasty uncle's secret.
explanation.definitionFit: To inform someone or fill them in is to tell them.

clue.text: One is given if 17 starts

parts.note: the player wearing shirt number one gets that number when picked to start; with a capital letter 'One' becomes the position's name in a team sheet

explanation.surface: A cryptic remark about what is handed out when a capital letter begins.
explanation.definitionFit: In football the number one shirt goes to the player guarding the net.

clue.text: They'd lure one travelling around British territory far away

indicators.note: around means surrounding, so the jumbled letters enclose the abbreviation
travelling suggests moving about, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Tempters lure someone on a journey to a distant British colony.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase names a remote, unknown distance or place, the distant sky or horizon.

clue.text: One had 20 x 2 parts to chuck out

indicators.note: parts means splits apart, so the eviction word is opened up to take the other letters

parts.note: to evict is to throw someone out
taken as written
2 refers to the answer at 2 down, and a con is a swindle, the same thing as that answer

explanation.surface: A mathematical-looking instruction about doubling a number and discarding pieces.
explanation.walkthrough: 20 is SENTENCE, so 'One had 20' is someone who served one. '2' points to 2 down, CHEAT, i.e. CON.
explanation.definitionFit: A former prisoner is someone who once served a prison term.

clue.text: Old individual in hire car from China, say?

indicators.note: in means placed inside, so the single letter goes within the word for hire car

parts.note: a rental is a hired car
I is the first-person individual, or one

explanation.surface: An elderly person in a rented car that came from China.
explanation.definitionFit: Eastern, as a description of Asia; China is an example, hence the question mark.

clue.text: London landlord's introduction to 20

parts.note: London is a capital city
a letter is one who lets property, a landlord

explanation.surface: A London pub landlord's opening remark.
explanation.walkthrough: 20 is SENTENCE; every written one begins with an upper-case letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Written statements start with an upper-case character, so it opens every one.

clue.text: Be in opposition's goal

definitions.meaning: to protest or disagree with something

explanation.surface: A political observation that resisting is the opposition party's aim.
explanation.definitionFit: As a verb it means protest; as a noun it means an aim, as in the object of the exercise.

clue.text: RAF target 1D?

parts.note: RAF pilots' slang for an enemy aircraft; such a villain also plays a minor role, as 1 down is BIT PARTS

explanation.surface: A question about what the air force aims at.
explanation.definitionFit: In RAF slang an enemy plane is called by the word for a robber or outlaw.

clue.text: Time? Or period following it?

definitions.meaning: a prison term, as in doing time
a full stop, called a period in the US, comes at the end of this grammatical unit

explanation.surface: A puzzled question about time and what comes after it.
explanation.definitionFit: It is both a prison term served and a grammatical unit ending in a full stop.

clue.text: Bottle still raised, runs in

indicators.note: in means placed inside, so the cricket abbreviation goes within the turned word
in a down entry, raised means the word for still is read upwards

parts.note: even can mean still, as in even better
R is the cricket abbreviation for runs

explanation.surface: A bottle is lifted while the runs come in.
explanation.definitionFit: Bottle is British slang for courage, and so is nerve.

clue.text: Reported leak that's thrilling

indicators.note: reported means spoken about, so the word is heard rather than read

parts.note: a leak and a wee are both slang for urinating

explanation.surface: News of a thrilling leak of information.
explanation.definitionFit: An exclamation of delight, as on a fairground ride, means something is exciting.

clue.text: What about "very good knock" as a memorial?

indicators.note: about means around, so the questioning word surrounds the other pieces

parts.note: eh is a questioning 'what?'
pi is slang for pious or very good
a tap is a light knock

explanation.surface: Someone wondering whether a phrase like 'very good knock' would suit a gravestone.
explanation.definitionFit: An inscription on a tomb commemorates the dead person, a kind of memorial.

clue.text: Clown both upright and corrupt

parts.note: a pier is a pillar or upright support
to rot is to decay or corrupt

explanation.surface: A clown who is both honest and crooked.
explanation.walkthrough: 'upright' looks like honest and 'corrupt' its opposite, but they are a pillar and decay.
explanation.definitionFit: A Pierrot is a sad clown figure from French pantomime, in white face and loose costume.

clue.text: What other earnings will keep behind

indicators.note: will keep means holds within, so the answer lies inside these clue words

explanation.surface: A question about which other income will be held back.
explanation.definitionFit: Placed at the back is the same as being behind.

clue.text: It should be great for surfing, dude

definitions.text: It should be great for surfing
definitions.meaning: a big rolling sea wave is what surfers want
a fashionable, stylish man, a dandy

explanation.surface: A surfer telling a friend the waves look great.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means both a large ocean wave and a smartly dressed man about town.
